definitions.explanation: Doing or expressing something in an undisguised, obvious way, often with a negative connotation suggesting a lack of tact or subtlety.

examples.japanese: {露骨|ろこつ}に⟦{無視|むし}→無視：13473_mushi⟧⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{傷|きず}ついた→傷つく：01934_kizutsuku⟧。
examples.english: I was hurt by being blatantly ignored.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{店員|てんいん}→店員：00897_tenin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧{露骨|ろこつ}に⟦{態度|たいど}を{変|か}える→態度を変える：22144_taidowokaeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{評判|ひょうばん}→評判：03586_hyouban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧。
examples.english: That shop clerk has a bad reputation because they blatantly change their attitude depending on the customer.

notes: Usually carries a negative or critical nuance, suggesting the person is being too obvious or lacking in social grace. Common collocations include {露骨|ろこつ}に⟦{嫌|いや}がる→嫌がる：03041_iyagaru⟧ (to openly show dislike), {露骨|ろこつ}な⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧ (a blatant attitude), and {露骨|ろこつ}な⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧ (explicit expression). The な-adjective form {露骨|ろこつ}な is equally common. Can also describe sexually explicit content: {露骨|ろこつ}な⟦{描写|びょうしゃ}→描写：05516_byousha⟧ (explicit depiction).
